# Job Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 417v–418r

---

**1** "Go ahead, cry out — will anyone answer you?
Which of the heavenly beings will you turn to?

**2** Resentment kills the fool,
and envy destroys the simple.

**3** I myself have seen a fool prospering,
but suddenly his home was cursed.

**4** His children have no one to protect them;
they are crushed in court with no defender.

**5** The hungry devour his harvest,
taking it even from among thorns,
and the thirsty swallow up his wealth.

**6** Hardship does not just spring up from the soil;
trouble does not sprout from the ground.

**7** But human beings are born for trouble
as surely as sparks fly upward.

**8** If I were in your place, I would appeal to God;
I would lay my case before him —

**9** the God who does great and unsearchable things,
wonders beyond counting.

**10** He sends rain upon the earth
and water upon the fields.

**11** He lifts up the lowly
and raises those who grieve to safety.

**12** He frustrates the schemes of the cunning,
so that nothing they attempt succeeds.

**13** He traps the clever in their own plots,
and the strategies of the devious collapse.

**14** They stumble around in darkness at midday,
groping at noon as if it were midnight.

**15** But God rescues the poor from their cutting words
and from the grip of the powerful.

**16** So there is hope for the helpless,
and the mouth of injustice is shut.

**17** How fortunate is the person whom God corrects!
Do not resent it when the Almighty disciplines you.

**18** For he wounds, but he also bandages;
he strikes, but his hands also heal.

**19** From six disasters he will rescue you;
in seven, no harm will touch you.

**20** In famine he will save you from death;
in battle, from the stroke of the sword.

**21** You will be safe from vicious slander,
and you will not be afraid when destruction comes.

**22** You will laugh at devastation and hunger,
and you will have no fear of wild animals.

**23** You will have a covenant with the very stones of the field,
and the wild animals will be at peace with you.

**24** You will know that your home is secure;
you will inspect your property and find nothing missing.

**25** You will know that your descendants will be many,
your offspring like the grass of the earth.

**26** You will go to your grave at a ripe old age,
like a sheaf of grain harvested at the proper time.

**27** We have examined this carefully, and it is true.
Listen to it, and apply it to yourself."

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The beautiful lie:** Eliphaz's speech in chapter 5 is theologically gorgeous and practically devastating. His vision of God (vv.9-16) — who sends rain, lifts the lowly, frustrates the wicked, and protects the poor — is beautiful. His promise of restoration (vv.17-26) reads like a psalm. The problem is that he is applying these truths to a situation they cannot explain. Everything Eliphaz says about God is true in general; none of it is true for Job in particular.

**"Born for trouble" (v.7):** This is one of the most fatalistic lines in the Hebrew Bible. If trouble is as natural as sparks flying upward, then Job's suffering requires no special explanation. But this directly contradicts the friends' other argument — that suffering is punishment for specific sin.

**"Examined this carefully" (v.27):** Eliphaz ends with the authority of tradition. The Hebrew literally says "we have searched it out." He speaks for the collective wisdom of generations. Job's radical contribution to the Bible is that he refuses to submit his experience to that collective certainty.

---
*— PNEUMA*
